<details><summary>About this simulation</summary>

The model has two teaching files, up to five local branches, and 50 commits. Switching branches requires a clean working tree here; real Git can carry non-conflicting edits. Diffs compare modeled settings, rather than whole files. `MM` indicates both staged and later unstaged changes; `UU` indicates an unresolved merge entry. Changing missions resets the simulated repository. Use [the real Git lab](git-lab.qmd) to practice in a terminal.

</details>

## Stuck? Read a worked route, then explain each move

<details><summary>Mission 1 · one decision per commit</summary>

Edit the rule to 0.50 and plot to purple. Run `git add config/analysis.toml`, compare `git diff --staged` with `git diff`, then `git commit -m "Compare a 0.50 s RT minimum"`. The commit contains the rule; purple remains only in working files. Try changing the rule after staging to see `MM`.

</details>

<details><summary>Mission 2 · shared base, independent changes</summary>

Create criteria at baseline; edit rule to 0.30, stage, commit. Switch main; edit plot purple, stage, commit. Merge criteria into main. The graph now has a merge with two parents because both branches advanced from c0. Each branch changed a different modeled file.

</details>

<details><summary>Mission 3 · a resolution is a staged decision</summary>

Create criteria; commit rule 0.30. Switch main; commit rule 0.25. Merge criteria. Inspect both versions and choose a final rule. Write the resolution, select and stage `config/analysis.toml`, then commit with a message such as "Resolve RT policy conflict after review". The model checks that resolution was staged even if you choose main's original value.

</details>

<details><summary>Mission 4 · local history and server history</summary>

Create criteria; change, stage, commit the rule; push criteria. Open the remote panel, open a PR, read its diff, record review, and merge. Switch local main, inspect its older tip, then pull --ff-only. For an extra challenge, let the labmate commit after review. Inspect why the merge now refuses until the new tips are reviewed.

</details>

<details><summary>Mission 5 · undo different kinds of changes</summary>

Edit and stage the rule; `git restore --staged config/analysis.toml` removes it from the index but preserves the working edit. Stage again and commit. `git revert HEAD` creates an inverse commit; the original remains in the graph. In this bounded model, revert supports only the latest single-parent commit.

</details>

## Command reference

| Command | Question it answers or action it takes |
| --- | --- |
| `git status` | Which branch, staged files, and unstaged files? |
| `git diff` / `git diff --staged` | Working versus index / index versus HEAD |
| `git add PATH` / `git add .` | Copy selected current working versions into the index |
| `git commit -m "Message"` | Record the index and move the current branch |
| `git switch -c criteria` / `git switch main` | Create and switch / switch an existing branch |
| `git merge criteria` / `git merge --abort` | Integrate into current branch / abandon unresolved merge |
| `git log --oneline --graph --all` | Inspect locally known history (console uses parent lists) |
| `git push -u origin criteria` | Share commits and update the server branch |
| `git fetch origin` | Update local knowledge of server pointers |
| `git pull --ff-only` | Fetch, then advance current branch if history permits |
| `git restore --staged PATH` | Unstage without discarding working edits |
| `git restore PATH` | Discard unstaged changes by restoring from the index |
| `git revert HEAD` | Add an inverse commit; preserve history |

Now complete [the real Git lab](git-lab.qmd). Close the command reference and explain, from memory, why committing, pushing, and opening a PR are three separate actions. Return in two days using [the practice plan](practice.qmd).
